correctness.rationale: Full proof reconstructs the singular Ito forward equation as u''-r|x|^alpha u=-r delta_b, two Bessel basis functions normalized at zero, constant Wronskian 2h and jump -r at the resetting point. Positive normalized invariant resolvent follows from resetting regeneration. For the decreasing solution q, E=q'^2-rx^alpha q^2 has E'=-r alpha x^(alpha-1)q^2<0 and E(infinity)=0, yielding strict logarithmic concavity and a unique radial peak. The growing right branch strictly increases. Therefore there are exactly two strict maxima with the stated pinning threshold. The opposite half-line probability follows by q''(x)=r x^alpha q(x), q'(infinity)=0. Extracted numerical verifier passed 112 assertions, but infinity results depend on proof.

originality.rationale: Closest primary literature explicitly supplies the centred Ito model and hitting transform (arXiv:2610.21962v1) and a nonzero-reset but different divergence-form heterogeneous generator (arXiv:2201.05598v1). Scientific premise/operator comparison is made at equation level. Broad Green method and prior special cases are credited. Independent priority validation remains outstanding.

value.rationale: Shifting the reset destination without shifting the physical mobility centre is a motivated experimental/control perturbation of the published Ito sluggish model. Its exact stationary law allows a structural all-parameter classification: precisely two peaks, a rate-dependent off-centre peak pinning event, and the opposite-side total population equal to one half an intrinsic hitting-before-reset probability. The threshold and crossing law are observable, not arbitrary chosen special parameters or routine numerical slices.
